sentences.text: Senior banking executives have told the BBC they expect the sector to be "on the menu" when the chancellor announces his Budget in two weeks' time.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: John Healey has described the banks as part of "the crown jewels" of the UK economy, yet has refused to rule out a raid on the sector.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: The biggest four banks collectively made around £15bn profit in the first six months of this year, leading to calls from trade unions and others for additional taxes.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: However, the banking sector trade body, UK Finance, warned that "further increases in bank taxes would weaken competitiveness, discourage investment and job creation, and work against the government's ambition to deliver growth in every postcode".
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: What is the Budget and what could be in it?
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: The UK's biggest banks and building societies currently pay a surcharge of 3% on top of the baseline 25% rate of corporation tax, plus a levy on the assets held on their balance sheets.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: The sector contributed nearly £40bn to the Treasury last year, if income tax on employees is factored in.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: The bank levy generated £1.4bn last year and the surcharge a further £1.2bn.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: There are a number of ways the chancellor could extract more money from the sector.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: The 3% surcharge was reduced from 8% under Rishi Sunak, at the same time as he raised corporation tax from 19% to 25%.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: Returning the surcharge to its previous level could raise around £2bn a year.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: The bank levy currently charges 0.1% on outstanding short-term loans and 0.05% on longer-dated loans, although mortgages are excluded from the calculation.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: In the past banks have successfully argued that higher taxes would risk making the UK uncompetitive with other jurisdictions and would reduce their ability to lend, and therefore be anti-growth.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: In truth, banks were pleasantly surprised they were not hit at the last Budget, given the large profits they have been making in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: Rising interest rates have expanded the margin between the rate at which they lend to customers and the rate they pay savers.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: There is another option that has been discussed with Treasury officials.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: Currently banks can use losses from the past to offset against profits - thereby reducing their tax bill in any given year.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: Lloyds in particular has been a beneficiary of this policy, as large losses from the financial crisis have been used to lower tax bills ever since.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: Some analysts and bank executives have pushed the idea of a moratorium on this practice for a few years, which would yield an estimated extra £1bn per year for the Treasury.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: That would provide a windfall while being "a lot more bearable", in the words of one bank executive.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: It would also spare foreign banks from an additional hit, including JP Morgan, whose chief executive Jamie Dimon has warned that the UK already has one of the highest tax burdens on banks in the world.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: He warned that adding further sector-specific taxes could discourage investment and damage competitiveness.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: However, industry leaders say any form of tax rise that hits UK banks and exempts foreign banks' operations in the UK would be hard to square with the government's push to back British business.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: Whatever form it takes, banks believe the chancellor now has much more of an appetite to take a larger slice of their pie.
sentences.article_title: Banks say Healey is planning Budget tax raid on their profits

sentences.text: This video can not be played Swimmer Archie Goodburn has been successful in his efforts to improve brain cancer care for patients as the UK government announce new measures.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Swimmer's emotional TV plea for cancer research leads to meeting with PM

sentences.text: The Scottish athlete, who was diagnosed with three inoperable brain tumours two years ago, met Prime Minister Andy Burnham after making an emotional plea on BBC Breakfast for more investment to be put into brain cancer research.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Swimmer's emotional TV plea for cancer research leads to meeting with PM

sentences.text: After the meeting, Burnham announced a new national brain cancer clinical lead and promised a review of brain cancer progress and action to get patients treatment sooner.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Swimmer's emotional TV plea for cancer research leads to meeting with PM

sentences.text: Goodburn, 25, thanked the prime minister and said all three of his requests have been "promised to some extent" but "fleshing out" needs to be done on the details.
sentences.article_title: Watch: Swimmer's emotional TV plea for cancer research leads to meeting with PM

sentences.text: The prime minister described the swimmer an "inspiration to us all" and said he was "delighted" to welcome him to Downing Street.

sentences.text: Trans patients should be cared for on single-sex hospital wards or bays that align with their biological sex rather than their gender identity, according to new NHS England (NHSE) guidance.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: It says when this is not "clinically appropriate" then alternative arrangements should be made and the dignity and safety of all patients should be maintained.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The guidance also says staff facilities should be used by people based on their biological sex, while trusts should ensure enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, such as single-occupancy toilets, are offered.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Previous NHSE guidance suggested patients and staff could be accommodated on wards or use facilities based on their gender identity.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: That meant that a trans woman – a biological male who identifies as a woman – could have chosen to be on a women's ward, or a trans man – a biological female who identifies as a man – could have opted for a men's ward.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: That guidance was withdrawn following the Supreme Court ruling in April 2025 that under equality law the term "sex" means biological sex and "woman" refers to a biological woman.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The judgment said for a space or service to be single sex it should only allow those of the same biological sex to use it.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Also under the new guidance issued on Thursday, NHSE emphasised that in order to avoid discriminating against trans people they should be offered gender neutral spaces.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: But the guidance also says decisions may have to be made on a case-by-case basis and must ensure clinical needs are met.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: It also makes clear that there are circumstances where clinical need is the overriding priority, including on emergency units and urgent care settings.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: In addition to the patient document of the guidance, NHSE has published advice for trusts on how to organise changing rooms, toilets and other single-sex facilities for staff.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Again, it says they should be used by people based on their biological sex, not their gender identity.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The document encourages NHS trusts in England to carry out an audit to ensure they are offering enough alternatives to single-sex facilities, for instance, gender neutral or single occupancy toilets.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Pressures on hospitals mean many have already struggled to keep wards single sex.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: NHSE data shows that the number of breaches of the previous mixed-sex accommodation guidance has been growing every year since 2021- where members of the opposite sex were placed on a single-sex ward.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: The most recent figure for August 2026 shows there were 5,520 breaches, compared to 3,853 in June 2025.
sentences.article_title: Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says

sentences.text: Louis, Otis and Ben all have differing opinions on whether teens should use protein powder Twelve-year-old Ben is desperate to try protein powder but there's one hurdle: me, his mum.

sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.text: A good rule of thumb is that the amount of protein you have for each meal should fit into the palm of your hand.
sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.text: But do teens really need it if they're eating well?
sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.text: For teenage boys and girls "you can get all the protein that you need from food alone", says registered dietitian Nichola Ludlam-Raine.
sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.text: It is important that teenage girls, especially, get enough iron and calcium, so Ludlam-Raine says not to become overly focused on protein at the expense of other nutrients.
sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.text: Protein shakes, powders or bars can be useful for some, including high-level athletes and those who have certain allergies, but they should not replace a healthy diet.
sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.text: There can also be some unwanted side effects from using protein powders such as bloating, gas, cramps, and diarrhoea.
sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.text: Those with pre-existing health conditions should not use it unless they have been told they can by their doctor.
sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.text: Ludlam-Raine points out that the protein powder market is not as tightly regulated as medicines.
sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.text: "Of course, you can get reputable companies who do third-party testing and make sure that what you see on the label is what is in the inside, but that's not always the case," she says.

sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.text: If you're keen to up your intake, try some of these recipes.
sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.article_title: My son wants to try protein powders - I asked experts how safe it was

sentences.text: "If you look at social media, they'll say you need to eat a lot of protein, but your body can handle only so much." He explains that if you eat too much, it has to be excreted by the kidneys and liver which can become overloaded.

sentences.text: In common with other AI firms, it is seeking to position itself as being able to generate huge profits despite spending billions on tech.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: It also emphasised safety at its event after warnings by current and former researchers of serious and even existential risks to humanity posed by AI.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: The company also told investors during the event at its headquarters in San Francisco that it had made a third quarter profit on an adjusted basis, an accounting method which ignores non-recurring costs.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: Investors reportedly left the Anthropic investor event optimistic about the company's rapid revenue growth and path to profitability.
sentences.article_title: AI giant Anthropic woos potential investors ahead of stock market debut

sentences.text: Marine ecology dog Sgiath at work A working dog from the Scottish Highlands has been named animal of the year by a charity for hunting down an invasive marine creature called the carpet sea squirt.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: This organism, also nicknamed "sea vomit", is particularly harmful to coastal wildlife and economies.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Working at low tide with her owner, Dr Texa Sim, black Labrador Sgiath has found hundreds of colonies of the sea squirt, which - if left uncontrolled - can smother and kill native species.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sgiath (pronounced Skee-ah) is thought to be the UK's first sea squirt-hunting dog.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Carpet sea squirt can be tricky to spot among seaweed "She's a natural," says Sim proudly.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: The International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) , external is awarding Sgiath animal of the years at its 26th annual animal Action Awards ceremony on Thursday 15 October.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sim, a marine ecologist based near Glencoe, has had Sgiath since she was a puppy and the bond between the two is strong.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: "Sgiath is incredibly clever.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Her problem solving and her ability to take on new challenges and learn so quickly are just phenomenal, and it's so amazing to watch." As a pup, Sgiath was trained as a mountain rescue dog.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: The Labrador proved to be so good that Sim wondered if she could use her skills to help with marine conservation work.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sgiath has been trained to recognise the scent of the carpet sea squirt.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: And now, the six year old joins her owner on the beaches to sniff it out.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sim says the dog is always right when pointing out a sea squirt, which can be difficult to spot, looking like slime among seaweed and on structures like pontoons and oyster cages.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Carpet sea squirt, or sea vomit, has spread to several places around the UK "When I first started this project, I genuinely didn't know whether it would work," said Sim.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: "No one had really explored whether dogs could help tackle this problem in the marine environment.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: It began as a proof-of-concept project and has exceeded every expectation I had." Dogs' scent detection skills are often used in conservation work on land, including tracking endangered species and helping investigate environmental crime.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: At low tide, Sgiath can, as Sim puts it "dive down under the seaweed".
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: "She just does a survey with her nose, essentially, she can pinpoint exactly where it is, so it's much easier," she said.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Marine experts believe that carpet sea squirt, formally named Didemnum vexillum, came from Japan.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: It arrived on the shores of the south of England and Wales in 2008.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: It can appear in various shades - from orange to cream -  and has now spread to several seaside locations across the UK.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: It reproduces quickly during the warmer summer months and, with warming seas, there are fears it could spread further.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Dr Martyn Kurr, a marine biologist from Bangor University told BBC News that non-native or "biofouling" species, like the carpet sea squirt, can outcompete native wildlife for valuable nutrients.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: "These species also clog up aquaculture pens, marine infrastructure, and machinery such as boat propellors," he explained.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Efforts to control and clean up these problematic marine invaders costs millions of pounds every year across Europe.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sgiath is also a trained mountain rescue dog To get Sgiarth proficient in both mountain rescue and marine conservation has needed hard work and long hours from both dog and owner.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: To locate and draw attention to a lost hiker on mountainous terrain, Sgiath is trained to bark and bounce around.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Conservation work requires a quieter approach.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sim explained that she trains Sgiath to give what's known as a "passive indication" when she finds the sea squirt.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: "It's a kind of a stillness, or a stare." Sgiath has been trained to stare when she finds carpet sea squirt When we speak to Sim over Zoom from her home, her two dogs are curled up in their beds at her feet.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Apparently, when Sgiath is not out finding lost people or marine creatures, she likes to be wrapped up in her dog blanket.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Sgiath, and Sim's younger Labrador Uisage, are both working dogs that are driven to do their jobs with treats and play.
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: Kurr, from Bangor University, said that scientists were just starting to realise that "these wonderful animals can smell changes in water that signal a marine invasion which otherwise might have gone unnoticed".
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: He added: "It's fantastic to see Sgiath get this much deserved award, and I'm very excited to see what other wonderful work we can do with sniffer dogs."
sentences.article_title: Dog that hunts invasive 'sea vomit' honoured as animal of the year

sentences.text: This video can not be played Challenge now is to safeguard UK economy's resilience, says chancellor The UK economy's stronger than expected performance in August has been called  a "sign of resilience" by Chancellor John Healey.
sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.text: Healey told the BBC "it's really tough in the face of these economic global shocks" as the latest official figures showed the economy grew by 0.1% for the month, defying analysts' forecasts of a slight contraction.

sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.text: Healey did not elaborate on what measures he will take in the Budget, but promised "where we can take action, we will".
sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.text: But, vowing to keep up the government's approach to fiscal discipline, Healey said "where we want to do things we have to make sure we can pay for them within the Budget that we've got and control spending".
sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.text: Over the three months to August, the UK's economy grew by 0.7% overall.
sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.text: ONS director of economic statistics Liz McKeown said computer programming had been the biggest contributor to what she described as "robust" growth over the period.
sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.text: But she said the production and construction sectors shrank over the three-month period.
sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.text: August's surprise expansion follows growth of 0.4% in July.
sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.text: Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said Britain's economy was "more robust than we thought".
sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.text: He warned that an expected increase in inflation would still "dampen growth", but added that the economy was showing "remarkable resilience to higher energy prices and borrowing costs".
sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.text: PwC senior economist Jake Finney said the development of AI infrastructure was underpinning Britain's relatively strong performance.
sentences.article_title: Healey says surprise UK growth is 'sign of resilience' ahead of Budget

sentences.text: "The UK still lags the US in both the scale of that investment and the boost it provides to growth, but it is making progress and remains ahead of many of its European peers," he added.

sentences.text: The official minimum rates of pay rose for 2.7 million workers on 1 April.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: The rate for workers aged 21 and over is called the National Living Wage, while those aged 18 to 20 are paid the National Minimum Wage.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: The rates apply across the UK.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: From 1 April 2026, workers over 21 on the National Living Wage are paid £12.71 an hour, 50p more than in 2025.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: For someone working full time (37.5 hours a week), that amounts to £24,784.50 a year -  an increase of £900.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: The rate for 18 to 20-year-olds has gone up to £10.85 an hour.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: That's an increase of 85p per hour.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: It amounts to an increase of £1,500 a year for a full-time worker.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: The government said its goal is to eventually scrap this separate rate for 18 to 20-year-olds, and have one rate for all adults.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: The minimum wage for 16 and 17-year-olds has also risen to £8 an hour.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: There are different rates of pay for apprentices , external depending on their age and what stage of apprenticeship they are in.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: Apprentices aged 16 to 18 are entitled to the National Minimum Wage rate for that age group which is currently £8.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: Those aged 19, or in the first year of their apprenticeship, are paid the same amount.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: But those over 19 - or who have already completed their first year - are entitled to the appropriate National Minimum Wage or National Living Wage rate for their age.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: What is an apprenticeship and how much is the pay?
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: Some workers do not qualify for either the National Minimum Wage or the National Living Wage.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: This includes the self-employed, company directors, volunteers, members of the armed forces and prisoners.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: People with disabilities or in long-term unemployment who take part in government work programmes are paid fixed amounts at different stages of the scheme.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: These are less than the equivalent National Minimum or Living rate.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: It is a criminal offence for employers not to pay the correct National Minimum and Living Wages to eligible employees.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.text: The rates apply even if workers are not paid by the hour.
sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.article_title: How much is the minimum wage?

sentences.article_title: Why are more roofs not made of solar tiles?

sentences.text: Choosing the right moment to harvest can be a make-or-break decision When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning." He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: How long do you have to pick it?" he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "That's where these models are really helpful." Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The firm is investing in technology with the hope of maximising productivity.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Even the apples are genetically engineered so that they don't brown easily once cut.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But planning a harvest is tricky.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: New tools that count and analyse fruit on the tree or vine, and predict when crops will ripen, are emerging.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: It matters because prices for fruit, especially high-value berries such as strawberries or blueberries can fluctuate wildly.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK .
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate).
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: We guarantee less than 20% error…" Angus Soft Fruits is one company that has worked with FruitCast.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Yasaman Ghasempour (left) is developing ripeness detection techniques Researchers are also exploring new ways of analysing fruit in intense detail.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Many farmers already use handheld brix meters to gauge the sugar content of their crop.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: These devices work by measuring how much light has changed direction, or refracted, after passing through a liquid – indicating the volume of solids present.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Some such meters use infrared light, meaning there's no need to cut into the fruit to take measurements.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But Yasaman Ghasempour at Princeton University says millimetre waves, high frequency radio waves, can penetrate deeper "They basically respond very well to humidity, water [and sugar]," she says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: She and her students have come up with a millimetre wave-based ripeness detector , external that could be used by farmers – or even customers searching for perfectly ripe fruit in shops.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Her students tried it out at a local market in New Jersey.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "[Staff] there got kind of scared that we were doing something shady," laughs Ghasempour.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Such fine-grained analysis of fruit, if currently unripe, could also help inform forecasts of when it will be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Jing Zhang says new tech has to prove its worth to farmers But while some growers, such as Carter, are interested in trying out new tech, many will wonder whether investing in it is really worthwhile.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Adoption is very complicated," says Jing Zhang at North Carolina State University.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "The grower has to have confidence in the research and whether or not it works." Zhang has been working on a system to automatically count the number of blueberries , external captured in smartphone images of blueberry bushes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The simplest systems need not be expensive.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Kevin Wang at the University of Florida has developed another crop-counting tool that can harvest imagery , external from $100 (£74) drones.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: In the future, such information could feed in to ripeness predictions.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: However, he points out that some farmers might be uneasy about sharing commercially sensitive information about their growing strategies, such as fertiliser and irrigation plans, with third parties and AI models.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Ben Palone is senior director of automation and commercialisation at Western Growers, an association that represents farmers in the western US.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He says harvest forecasts have some potential as "an optimisation tool".
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But farmers will likely continue to rely on human intelligence.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Growers like to have people in the mix to make some of those very critical decisions – especially when it comes to harvests," he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Europe's heatwave has boosted demand for battery storage systems As heatwaves scorched Europe this summer, workers at a US battery company noticed an uptick in demand.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: San Diego-based Unigrid sells a nine kilowatt hour battery for people's homes.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sweltering European homeowners were apparently looking for ways of storing power when it was available from the grid at lower rates.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They could then run air conditioners more cheaply, off the battery, during the worst heat of the day.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We have requests coming from Spain, France, Germany, The Netherlands," says Darren Tan, co-founder and chief executive.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've shipped the first 100 units and [expect to ship] 1,000 before the end of the year." Unigrid's battery is an emerging technology – it's a sodium ion, rather than lithium ion device.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries have got energy storage experts excited because they could end up much cheaper to build and operate than lithium ion.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: They're potentially less likely to catch fire and should also work in a wider range of temperatures, even down to lows of minus 40C , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Darren Tan founded Unigrid - a maker of sodium ion batteries But there's a debate over what constitutes the best, and safest, sodium ion battery design.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Plus, more than one , external US company working in this space has floundered in recent years , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: China leads the world in sodium ion battery manufacturing at present so US competitors are going to have to work hard to keep up.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The prize that awaits is the possibility of batteries made in the US with 100% US-sourced materials.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is unlike lithium ion batteries, where China dominates the materials , external supply chain as well as manufacturing.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: For Tan, China has helped his company get to market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The Unigrid battery currently uses sodium ion cells made there, rather than in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We can switch back and forth and choose what battery we want to work with," says Tan, explaining that, in future, his firm might source cells from the US – though these may come at a different cost.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: There's another consideration.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Unigrid's battery contains chromium-3 in its cathode.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In a battery, electrons flow from cathode to anode , external when charging and in the opposite direction when discharging or providing power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Ivana Hasa, at the Warwick Manufacturing Group, University of Warwick, who has no connection to Unigrid, agrees that it is possible for chromium-3 to form chromium-6 at very high states of charge, though she says this can be mitigated by how voltage is controlled within the battery.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "Safety tests reported on the cell chemistry are very promising," she says of Unigrid's tech.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Tan says concerns around toxicity of the battery's materials are "overblown" and emphasises that Unigrid's battery has passed certification and safety tests for sale in Europe and is currently undergoing such evaluations for the US market.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Third-party tests have not been able to get the battery to form chromium-6, he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We've tried very hard to try and produce it, we've overcharged it as much as we can...
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: We were unsuccessful in generating chromium-6." The choice of cathode material, or how the electrolyte – which separates cathode and anode – is formulated are key details influencing the performance and longevity of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some manufacturers are not using chromium for their cathode but hard carbon instead, or sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (NFPP).
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: In general, confidence around sodium ion batteries' reliability has increased during the last few years, says Prof Dame Grey, meaning they are now finding their way into grid storage applications.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Last December, LFP batteries – a relatively cheap form of lithium ion battery – were trading at $81 per kilowatt hour , external (kWh) whereas Unigrid's sodium ion battery pricing is roughly $100 kWh , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Some companies that spoke to the BBC suggested sodium ion might reach as low as $30 per kWh but analysts say significantly lower costs could be many years away , external .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Sodium ion batteries are also not as energy dense as lithium ion batteries, meaning they must be slightly bigger and heavier in order to provide the same amount of power.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The technology has been improving , external on this front in recent years but, even so, you're not likely to see sodium ion cells in small, energy hungry devices such as smartphones.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Larger energy storage solutions are where most people expect sodium ion to dominate.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Emerald Battery Labs founders (left to right) Aric Stocks, Kjell Schroder, David Bell "We think sodium ion […] is going to make up 80% of the market," says David Bell, co-founder and chief executive of Seattle-based Emerald Battery Labs.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Bell declined to share details of the battery design his firm is working on, though he says Emerald too is currently relying on China-sourced sodium ion cells as they develop their initial product: 12 volt auxiliary batteries for vehicles, currently supplied to unnamed commercial fleets in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "We took a look at the market and said 'Hey, no-one's trying to attack this space, let's have Emerald Battery Labs attack it'," says Bell.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The firm's next goal is to develop new anodes for US-produced sodium ion cells.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Another company, Peak Energy, based in California and Colorado, announced a partnership with General Motors (GM) in June.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The pair aim to develop a US supply chain for sodium ion batteries, in order to enable large-scale energy storage for electricity grids.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Peak Energy is also, at present, relying on China-sourced cells for its first installations, but hopes to help GM launch a US-based production facility in Michigan "by the end of 2028", says Cameron Dales, president and co-founder.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "China does not have an insurmountable lead in sodium ion batteries," he says.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Alysm sodium ion batteries are made in the US One reason US companies feel they can compete is because of the electricity demand boom from data centres, which are contributing to rising greenhouse gas emissions in the US.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Data centre-driven demand is also rising in other places around the world, including the UK .
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: This is an "opportunity" says Drew Buckley, chief executive at ESS Tech, headquartered in Oregon.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: He points out that sodium ion batteries could help distribute renewable energy to data centres.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And those batteries should be cheaper to run than lithium ion alternatives, since they are not expected to require as much cooling.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: ESS Tech is working with Alsym, another US firm that is planning to ship "hundreds" of megawatt hours' worth of sodium ion batteries – made in the US – by 2027.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: Hasa says that it will be "challenging" for companies to establish mass production of sodium ion batteries.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: And she also notes that, while this type of battery is often touted as much safer than lithium ion, they do not come with zero fire risk.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: But if any firms can succeed in this space, they could enable new strategic choices, she adds – helping to avoid wastage of renewable electricity and potentially keeping energy costs low.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: "I'm a strong believer in the technology," says Hasa.
sentences.article_title: The start-ups hoping to return battery making to the US

sentences.text: The long nose of the X-59 is designed to dampen the plane's sonic boom There's a weird and wonderful jet flying over the US.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It has the nose of anteater, parts cannibalised from other planes and a cockpit so far back the pilot depends on a camera to see where he's going.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: This contraption, the X-59, might just be the future of air travel.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-59's owes its eccentric design to the problem of sonic booms.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The shockwave created by a jet breaking the sound barrier restricted Concorde to flights over the sea and barred it from lucrative routes across the US.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Now Nasa is working around that problem using the X-59's elongated snout to flatten supersonic booms into tolerable bumps in the background.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: On top of its bizarre appearance the X-59 boasts a remarkable lineage.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It's the latest in a series of experimental Nasa aircraft dating back to 1947 and the first plane to break the sound barrier, the Bell X-1.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Peter Coen, a 43-year Nasa veteran who manages the programme, explains the thinking behind 80 years of X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "Our approach is to pick small goals we aim to prove with flight data and we construct an airframe for that one task." The X-plane philosophy is to "minimise goals, the more goals you have the more expensive it gets." For the X-59 it's about suppressing sonic booms on a budget and nothing else.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In the case of the X-1, flown through the sound barrier in 1947 by the legendary test pilot Chuck Yeager, Nasa knew a .50 calibre bullet travelled faster than the speed of sound.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: So the stumpy little aircraft was shaped like a bullet with wings added.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A mere 20 years later the X-15 rocket plane, a cylinder with tiny wings dropped from a B-52 bomber, flew to 6.7 times the speed of sound (4,520 mph) and the edge of space, paving the way for heat-resistant materials vital to the Space Shuttle.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In 1947 the Bell X-1 was the first plane to break the sound barrier Nasa will fly the X-59 in conjunction with community surveys to assess what people think when a supersonic boom is bent by the planes stretched nose and hushed up.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "We want to figure out what level of boom is acceptable to people on a regular basis," says Coen, who reckons his machine will sound "like a car door being closed across the street" when it flies past Mach 1, around 660mph at airline cruising altitude.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: With its cockpit and ejector seat taken from a T-38 training jet, its landing gear from an F-16 fighter and engine courtesy of the F-18 this jigsaw of an aircraft was assembled by Lockheed Martin for Nasa.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A camera feeding a screen in front of the pilot relies on instantaneous computer processing to get round the lack of forward vision.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It first flew in 2025, has gone supersonic and will break the sound barrier over chosen US towns in 2027.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: But is there still a place for X-plane projects in a world where relatively cheap drones are being rapidly developed - not least in Ukraine's war against Russia .
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Even Nasa considered an uncrewed X-59.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: But drones are not always a cheaper option.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Removing the pilot would have added the cost and complication of certifying a robot jet to fly fast over urban areas.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Plus the X-59 had to be big enough to resemble an airliner punching through the sound barrier, which in turn allowed space for a cockpit.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Nasa is no stranger to drone X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-48, a scaled down model of an airliner that blends wing and fuselage to create a single lifting body, flew in 2007.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Small was beautiful for the tiny X-48 with its 20ft wingspan as this kept the programme within budget.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Within months they realised their system could work much faster than anything they had seen before.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Eighteen months in and we actually have a completely functional, super high-performance simulator," says Lu.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The software is so efficient that it can run on the hardware carried by Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That means the robot can run tens of thousand of simulations while it is moving around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It can look about a second, or so, ahead into the future for 20,000 different kind of combinations of things that might happen," Storey explains.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And that would be vital for a robot moving around an unstructured environment like the average home.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Things outside of the robot's control, like humans, animals or even other robots, could do things that require a change of strategy.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: These unexpected events could happen very quickly and the robot needs to be able to quickly adapt to ensure its actions remain safe and on-mission," Lu says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Robot training systems use virtual environments where tasks are practised Vsim is a start-up with 10 engineers working on its tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It does not build robots, instead it has a suite of software designed to let organisations train and control robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The problem is when you start doing long-horizon tasks, where I say: 'I want you to take the bottle and I want you to fill it up and I want you to go pour'," says Spencer Huang, director of product for robotics at Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: This year Nvidia has started using AI agents to help build virtual environments to train robots and validate whether the solutions from training work or not.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "When we talk about creating the [virtual] world and actually scanning it in - a lot of that is actually manual labour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "We're just throwing agents at it... it's basically given us a huge workforce," Huang says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Simulation is not the only method for training robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: They can also be trained by watching human or video demonstrations.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Rika Antonova has spent more than a decade working in robotics Rika Antonova has been working in the field of robotics since 2015 and is currently an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Her research is focused on , external developing software and hardware that can aid robots to learn complex behaviour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Antonova works with a training system called MuJoCo, owned by Google's DeepMind since 2021.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's open-source software, which means researchers can use it for free, and are allowed to tinker with the code.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It is very, very user-friendly.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: So for research groups or for small start-ups, that's useful," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: She says that Vsim's approach - very fast simulation - is promising.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "If you have a very, very fast simulator, then you can simulate hundreds of millions of samples in that few seconds that your robot is thinking about how to adjust its motion, and then you can change the motion almost in real time," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But those simulated environments are still rough approximations of the real world, which limits what can be trained.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "There are certain things that are hard to model in simulation, like highly deformable objects and cutting," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's a challenge that Nvidia and Lu and Storey at Vsim are working on.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says their system has "reduced approximation, using accurate simulations to train models that genuinely work in reality as well as they do in simulations." Soon a second robot, to be called Nacho, will be helping develop that tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says that should speed up their development process and ensure their software can run on different machines.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And, of course, provide Freddo with some company.

sentences.text: Around 650 more prisoners in England and Wales are due to be released under the second tranche of the government's early release scheme.

sentences.text: The review looks at NHS waiting times and whether young people are being over-diagnosed.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: It has been called a "generational opportunity" to rethink support for both mental health conditions and ADHD and autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The review, commissioned by then-health secretary Wes Streeting 10 months ago after saying young people were being "over-diagnosed" and "written off", could have major implications for NHS services, the benefits system, schools and employment support.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Its 600-plus pages , external contain a host of conclusions and recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Here are the key takeaways.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The report is clear that there is an increasing risk of over-diagnosis, but only when it comes to ADHD and autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Experts said a rise in diagnoses over the past 25 years meant cases now appear to be outstripping the expected number in the population for some younger age groups.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: They gave the example of children aged six to 17 – more than 4% have been diagnosed with autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: That's well above the 1-2% that studies suggest is the true level.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But this comes with a big caveat.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: There are weaknesses in the data.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Evidence about the true level of autism relies on surveys that have not been done for nine years, so the review team have had to estimate what has happened since.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: And there are some age groups where these conditions are still being under-diagnosed, and that should not be overlooked.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: It is why the review team said it could not yet conclude over-diagnosis was happening "at scale".
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But there is certainly evidence to suggest we are moving from an era of under-diagnosis to one of over-diagnosis, the experts said.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: They warn not every difficulty requires a medical response and there is a risk of blurring the lines between diagnosable ADHD and autism and what should be considered the "normal human variation in brain function, cognition and behaviour".
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Where the review team very clearly rejects the idea of over-diagnosis is with mental health.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: In fact, the chair, Prof Peter Fonagy, has said Streeting was "completely wrong" on that.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: He said the increase in mental distress is real – one in four 16 to 24-year-olds are now thought to experience it, up from one in six 30 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: He links this to a variety of factors including economic uncertainty, the impact of social media and loss of youth services.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: This contrasts with autism and ADHD.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: While diagnoses have increased, the true level in the whole population (regardless of whether they have come forward or not) has remained broadly stable, according to best estimates.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: What is not happening with mental health, though, is an increase in severe mental illness.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Population rates of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, for example, have remained stable.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Instead, what is driving the rise is conditions such as anxiety, depression, self-harm and eating disorders.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Where the review experts share, to some extent, Streeting's concerns is on the impact of diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: They said there was a risk it ends up closing doors to opportunities.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: It can, they said, act as a label that defines them by their "difficulties" rather than "strengths and potential".
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: This then hampers them in education, work and relationships.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Around a third of 16 to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training (NEET) report their mental health or autism as a factor.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Those diagnosed with ADHD before the age of 17 are four times more likely to be a NEET than those without.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Addressing this, they said, would require better support post-diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Some of that is down to the NHS, but as important is the approach of schools, workplaces and wider society.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Another area where the review team is united in its view is that the support system is "falling short" of what people need for both mental health and neurological conditions such as ADHD and autism.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Waiting times for assessment are too long.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: A third of young people referred to mental health services wait more than a year, while of the 900,000 people waiting for ADHD or autism checks, 90% have waited more than three months.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: In the lead up to publication of the report, NHS Alliance, which represents health bosses, said the system was in chaos.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But this goes further than the NHS.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The report said support across care, education, employment and welfare remains fragmented, with people having to "jump through hoops" and face repeated assessment and conflicting requirements to get support.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: No time should be wasted in tackling these challenges, the review says.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: On long waits, it says everyone on a waiting list should be reassessed so that those most in need are prioritised for help.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: There should no longer be a first-come, first-served approach.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Some of those waiting may benefit from non-medical support, advice about sleeping better or getting more physical exercise, for example.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: That may even lead to some being removed from the waiting list.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: There should also be better assessments before people are placed on waiting lists too.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Not every problem needs a medical solution, the experts make clear.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Quality and consistency of autism and ADHD assessments must be improved, with the review highlighting concerns about those done by the private sector on behalf of the NHS.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: Half of ADHD and a third of autism assessments are done by non-NHS providers, such as charities and private firms.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: But they are not subject to the same regulation as NHS providers – and this must change.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The experts also said it wanted to see a ban on direct-to-public advertising of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The review has said it wants to see action over the next 12 to 24 months.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know

sentences.text: The government has promised to act – and is expected to set out more details in its forthcoming mental health strategy which is expected by the end of the year.
sentences.article_title: Autism, ADHD and mental health review: What you need to know
