sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Caroline Bailey says she has completed several goals on her "tick list" since being diagnosed, including travelling to Italy and moving to a cottage in Wales When Caroline Bailey was suffering with sharp, stabbing pains in her stomach, she thought it was being caused by her contraceptive coil.

sentences.article_title: My contraceptive coil saved my life after it revealed I had cancer

sentences.article_title: My contraceptive coil saved my life after it revealed I had cancer

sentences.article_title: My contraceptive coil saved my life after it revealed I had cancer

sentences.article_title: My contraceptive coil saved my life after it revealed I had cancer

sentences.article_title: My contraceptive coil saved my life after it revealed I had cancer

sentences.article_title: My contraceptive coil saved my life after it revealed I had cancer

sentences.article_title: My contraceptive coil saved my life after it revealed I had cancer

sentences.article_title: My contraceptive coil saved my life after it revealed I had cancer

sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Felicity Gillespie, chief executive of Kindred Squared, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that children not being potty trained when starting school was "a real concern for teachers".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "They tell us that they're losing, on average across the country, a day a week of teaching time to dealing with potty-training issues." Gillespie is keen to spread the message that "it's best for children to be coming out of nappies" when they are between 18 and 30 months old.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When the teacher's leaving the class to change someone's nappy, the rest of the class is having their learning broken up.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So everybody loses out,” she added.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The ability to listen to and follow instructions is another skill that helps pupils get the most out of learning when they start reception class Jo Mould, who teaches reception at Robert Wilkinson Primary Academy in York, said she has noticed an improvement in pupils being ready for school this year.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "We've spent more time teaching in these last three weeks than we have in previous years," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "The children have come in so ready to learn, because they're more settled and regulated socially and emotionally.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: We've had a really, really positive start to the school year." Jo Mould says not having to deal with toilet training has meant more time spent teaching her pupils York councillor Bob Webb said the impact of the scheme had been "so positive" for both schools and families.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: But he acknowledged a potential "gap in support" for parents between seeing health visitors with their toddler, and the child later arriving at school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: He said the key to the scheme's success was collaboration across health visitors, schools and other community settings, but that there was "always more that could be done at an earlier age".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Twenty local authorities across England have now committed to adopt York's model, developed by Kindred Squared, and use it to encourage earlier potty-training in their areas.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: That means they were assessed by teachers on being able to complete tasks like going to the toilet and paying attention in class.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The government has said it is still committed to increasing that proportion to 75% by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Early Education Minister Paul Waugh said it was "encouraging to see this pilot helping more children develop the confidence and independence they need before starting school", stressing the importance of parents taking early steps towards toilet training.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: In York, Mould said she hopes next year's parents will take on potty-training even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "Ideally we'd be at the point where [children] don't need that support when they get here, because they've already been trained by the time they get to us." Do you have any views, comments or questions about this story?

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: But in a hearing in February, the woman, who was referred to as Jane, told the judge she had lied about the pregnancies for revenge, claiming the man had abused her.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Following this, the woman sent a message to his stepfather saying the baby had been born as well as sharing baby photos.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman would go on to tell the man's mother the baby had been born.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman admitted to the court she had told him she was pregnant when they were together, and afterwards, but conceded she had told a series of elaborate lies and that there were, in fact, no children.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She argued she was menopausal at the time and could not have been pregnant and bank statements show she attended a tanning shop on the day she said she had given birth, Mrs Justice Judd said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In her judgement, the judge concluded that the "factors that weigh against the children genuinely existing were very strong, stronger than the factors pointing the other way".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She said the man was the victim of a "sustained and elaborate campaign of deceit" which also impacted his mother and closest friend.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: "Added to this, the behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.", the Judge said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The judge added she was unable to conclude the woman's motive for her behaviour but said financial fraud was a "possibility"  and that the "complex mental health problems" she suffered from may have also played a part.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Former minister Alan Milburn says children as young as four should be learning about different careers, with work experience placements made mandatory for 14- to 16-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: However, teaching unions warn of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools and say practical considerations must ensure all schools have access to the support.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training (known as Neet), between April and June 2026.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn told the BBC "in primary school, it's really about opening their eyes and giving them a sense about what is possible".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Despite a push towards apprenticeships and work experience in Years 10 and 11, for many the journey towards becoming Neet starts well before their 16th birthday.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: As a result, Milburn says children should be introduced to the world of work much earlier in their school journey, with dedicated space in the curriculum to "broaden horizons".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The final instalment of Alan Milburn's review into Neets is due to be published this autumn He told the BBC this could be achieved by employers giving talks in primary schools and offering taster sessions to children.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "It'd be good if employers came into schools and said, 'Look, this is what's going on, these are things that are possible.'" Milburn says that for Key Stage 4 pupils - aged between 14 and 16 - experience must be given in a real workplace with employer feedback.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Work experience needs to be mandatory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: It makes a big difference," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn also emphasised the difficulty some young people face when trying to find work experience placements.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "There are about four in ten people aged 14-16 who aren't getting any work experience at all," he said.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Education is devolved in the UK, so while Milburn's review looks at the picture in all four nations, his recommendations regarding education are specific to England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Currently in England, careers guidance must be offered to students aged 11-18 and work experience is not statutory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The government has said its vision , external is to "guarantee two weeks' worth of work experience for every young person" in England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: In both Scotland and Wales, career-based learning is already a requirement in schools for students as young as three.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Emma, from Kirklees, has grandchildren in Years 1, 2 and 4 and thinks primary school is too young to be introducing careers talks.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "In primary school, there is too much trying to get little kids to grow up too quickly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Just let them be little kids.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: I know they have to learn and the world's changing, but still, give them a chance to be kids." But Zoe, another parent, disagrees.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "I think it's a good idea," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of school leaders' union National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT), warns of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Whenever new mandatory requirements are proposed, it is important to be clear about what might have to give way to make room for them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Whiteman also highlights the value of existing programmes such as "Primary Futures", which bring in volunteers from different professions into schools to "challenge stereotypes and raise aspirations".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "The earlier young people can begin to make connections between what they learn in school and the possibilities that lie ahead, the better," Whiteman says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL), says having someone come into the classroom can really "enlighten [children's] motivation... and give them that sense of passion for all the opportunities beyond the classroom".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Although he acknowledges that finding opportunities in rural areas could be more challenging.

sentences.text: A second head teachers' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections in England, saying it is "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale" of its members.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) also raised the prospect of potential strike action, saying a new grading system had become an "overbearing mess".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: On Friday, Ofsted's chief inspector Sir Martyn Oliver said an independent survey of education providers showed it was "on the right track" with inspections.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: The Department for Education (DfE) said ministers were "working with Ofsted and school leaders to ensure accountability is fair, proportionate and focused on helping every school get better".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: ASCL said it had passed a motion of no confidence in "the ability of Ofsted's leadership to address the damage being done by the new inspection system", adding that it was "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale of members".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary, said the union did not take the step "lightly", but added Ofsted's "warm words about recognising wellbeing pressures... have not been matched by the action necessary" and that "negotiation [had] hit a brick wall".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: "The current system is not fit for purpose.

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: All three companies have appeared in court this week, arguing they should not need to provide so much information in response to Ofcom's formal requests.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta has separately also argued Ofcom should not be able to levy fines for breaches based on its global annual revenue.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: It also contends that its messaging and image-sharing apps should not have to face additional requirements under the OSA, such as tackling paid-for fraud ads.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Little terns first came to Seaton Carew in 2019 A little tern colony has experienced its toughest breeding season since establishing themselves at a site.
sentences.article_title: Little tern colony has worst breeding season

sentences.text: Since 2019 the seabirds have travelled about 3,000 miles (4,828km) from West Africa to Seaton Carew, near Hartlepool.
sentences.article_title: Little tern colony has worst breeding season

sentences.text: But this year the colony's 83 nesting pairs produced just 17 fledglings, compared to 67 in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Little tern colony has worst breeding season

sentences.text: Tees Valley Wildlife Trust said flooding and damage to the colony's perimeter fence contributed to difficult conditions for the birds.
sentences.article_title: Little tern colony has worst breeding season

sentences.text: The protective fencing around the nesting ground was washed away in high tides earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Little tern colony has worst breeding season

sentences.text: Lead warden Derek Wood said a late arrival of their inshore food supply as well as predation also contributed to the birds' tough season.
sentences.article_title: Little tern colony has worst breeding season

sentences.text: In June, it was reported numbers were down 50%, which the team attributed to dogs being inside the exclusion zone.
sentences.article_title: Little tern colony has worst breeding season

sentences.text: Tees Valley Wildlife Trust is looking at how to make the 2027 breeding season more successful "The season has been a difficult one for the dedicated wardens and volunteers who work tirelessly to protect the colony," Wood said.
sentences.article_title: Little tern colony has worst breeding season

sentences.text: But the team is hopeful the colony can bounce back when they return from Africa in spring, with plans to improve the site and further protect the birds under way.
sentences.article_title: Little tern colony has worst breeding season

sentences.text: An emotional scene of an elephant carrying a deceased calf has earned Italian photographer Federico Veronesi the title of Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026.
sentences.article_title: Pictured: Winning entries for Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026

sentences.text: While tracking elephants in Namibia's Huab River Valley, Veronesi spotted an unusual trail of drag marks across the sand of a dry riverbed.
sentences.article_title: Pictured: Winning entries for Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026

sentences.text: Following the tracks, he came across a female elephant carrying a dead calf, its leg wedged between her tusk and trunk.
sentences.article_title: Pictured: Winning entries for Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026

sentences.text: Initially, Veronesi assumed the elephant was the calf's mother.
sentences.article_title: Pictured: Winning entries for Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026

sentences.text: But after sharing his photographs with an elephant research project working in the area, he learned that this wasn't certain.
sentences.article_title: Pictured: Winning entries for Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026

sentences.text: Researchers recognised the elephant as a female who had lost a calf several years earlier and said she had previously picked up dead calves belonging to other females.
sentences.article_title: Pictured: Winning entries for Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026

sentences.text: For Veronesi, the encounter was deeply significant.

sentences.text: Elon Musk has suggested that the US government may be behind restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to SpaceX's Starlink internet network.
sentences.article_title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds

sentences.text: Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and also protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said unexpected new speed limits were disrupting its battlefield missions.
sentences.article_title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds

sentences.text: An adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky said he believed the restrictions were not a coincidence and were related to the latest strains between Kyiv and Washington.
sentences.article_title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds

sentences.text: Musk said that Starshield, the military-grade sister service to Starlink, is controlled by the US government, and "any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately [the US president]".
sentences.article_title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds

sentences.text: Musk - writing on X - had been responding to pleas from Ukrainian officials to restore connectivity, including from Zelensky who told UK media: "I hope that it's a mistake, maybe [a] huge technical problem.
sentences.article_title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds

sentences.text: I don't know, but we are asking to... switch [it] on." Starlink, which is owned by Musk's SpaceX, restricted speed limits on Tuesday night to 100mph (160km/h), meaning any weapons that travelled faster than that lost connectivity to the network.
sentences.article_title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds

sentences.text: It had been partially restored by Wednesday evening, Ukraine's former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov said.
sentences.article_title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds

sentences.text: "Removing Starshield's speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine's defense," he wrote on X, thanking Elon Musk and asking for his "continued support".

sentences.text: About an hour later, Musk replied to that post, defending his company's involvement.
sentences.article_title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds

sentences.text: "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government.

sentences.text: Dermot Gethings is vice chair of the Preston & District Astronomical Society Nearly 54 years ago, Apollo 17 blasted off from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, bound for the moon.

sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Ahead of the screening of a documentary about his experience, Preston astronomer Dermot Gethings recalled how, at 16 years old, he was hand picked by the United States embassy and Nasa to witness the launch.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "As it launched there was this incredible adrenaline and a shockwave that rattled every bone in your body," said the now 70-year-old of the events of 7 December 1972.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "It is the stuff that you dream about." Dermot Gethings with Neil Armstrong at the Miami motel the pair stayed at ahead of the Apollo 17 launch While Gethings grew up in Frenchwood in Preston, he was shaped by the ongoing Cold War Space Race and the quest to put a man on the moon.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: A childhood of sci-fi, The Thunderbirds and televised Nasa missions meant space was always a keen interest of his.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: He said the "trigger moment" for his lifelong interest in astronomy was seeing the Milky Way in the night sky when he was 10.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "It hit me straight away - that was where I wanted to be," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "And I took a deep interest in space." From then on Gethings started an astronomy club at the former St John Fisher's School in Preston - putting on talks both at his school and others and running public exhibitions.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Gethings got an O-Level in Astronomy, at age 16, after teaching himself the curriculum at home After Gethings' exhibitions were photographed by the Lancashire Evening Post, his life changed forever.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "A few months after the photographs were published I received a letter out of the blue from the United States Embassy in London," he recalled.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "It said 'We have a very special project to discuss with you regarding the forthcoming Apollo 17 mission'." Gethings was then told he was one of 16 UK students being invited for an interview at the embassy.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Gethings pictured in front of the White House on 5 December 1972 A memorable moment for Gethings came when he accidentally met Armstrong - the first man to have ever walked on the moon.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "On the day of the launch I stepped out of my motel room and clumsily walked into a tall gentleman," Gethings recalled.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "I stood on his foot by accident and I was really embarrassed.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "I looked up and the man smiling down at me was Neil Armstrong!" The pair walked downstairs together chatting about the upcoming launch, before Armstrong offered for his wife to take a photograph of them.

sentences.text: They were only three miles (5km) away from the launchpad.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "My heart was pumping in my chest," he remembered.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "And when the vehicle cleared the tower suddenly you got punched in the chest by a shockwave.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "The ground beneath your feet was like an earthquake and the stands were rattling.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "And then you got hit by this incredibly painful crackling staccato snapping sound  against the skin on your face.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "Minutes later Apollo 17 became a bright star moving across the sky and away from us.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: The winner of a prestigious scientific photography competition has been disqualified following concerns raised by other scientists that it was fake.

sentences.text: Nikon said the use of generative AI in the composition of the video broke the rules of its Small World In Motion contest, which accepts photos and video taken using powerful microscopes.
sentences.article_title: Prize-winning image which sparked backlash was AI-generated, Nikon rules

sentences.text: The firm said the video "did not comply with the competition rules regarding generative AI", but added it was not a judgement of the entrant's professional reputation or scientific contributions.
sentences.article_title: Prize-winning image which sparked backlash was AI-generated, Nikon rules

sentences.text: It said it would now look at the rules and procedures of the annual contest, which has been running for 15 years and is specifically for microscopic images.
sentences.article_title: Prize-winning image which sparked backlash was AI-generated, Nikon rules

sentences.text: Nikon said it came to the decision "after thoroughly re-evaluating the video and supporting materials and consulting with members of our judging panel".
sentences.article_title: Prize-winning image which sparked backlash was AI-generated, Nikon rules

sentences.text: The winning entry came from Dr Ning Xu, from Tsinghua University in China, who submitted a short video showing tiny, hair-like structures called cilia moving in the airway of a child with the respiratory condition PCD.
sentences.article_title: Prize-winning image which sparked backlash was AI-generated, Nikon rules

sentences.text: The BBC has approached him for comment.
sentences.article_title: Prize-winning image which sparked backlash was AI-generated, Nikon rules

sentences.text: A number of scientists, including former competition judges, complained to Nikon on its LinkedIn page that the video did not appear to be real.
sentences.article_title: Prize-winning image which sparked backlash was AI-generated, Nikon rules

sentences.text: Xu had acknowledged using AI, but said he believed he had acted within the rules, and had cooperated with Nikon's investigation.

sentences.text: University of Leicester scientist Dr Robert Hirst, who was among the first experts to voice concerns, said he was "not surprised" and he "knew immediately that the video was fabricated".

sentences.text: "I have been diagnosing PCD for 20 years by examining their cilia waveform, length, cell size and shape," he said.

sentences.text: Hirst, who is lead scientist for the NHS centre for PCD diagnosis at the university, said the cells and cilia "look nothing like those from PCD patients".

sentences.text: Drone pilot Pete Short hunts for hotspots in the Cairngorms National Park which was devastated by a huge wildfire over the summer It is 06:00 and I'm meeting drone pilot Pete Short for a dawn patrol in the Cairngorms National Park.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: It is a job he has been doing for almost three months, since a huge wildfire tore through this landscape in July.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: The flames which swept across the hillsides are gone.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: From where we are standing, there is little to suggest there is still a fire here at all.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: But that is exactly what we have come to find.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: After a bumpy drive into the woodland, Pete launches a thermal drone into the early morning sky.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: I am given a job too: keeping the aircraft in sight while he studies the images being sent back to his screen.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "Every week I hope that I find none," he tells me.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "On the last thermal flight I did we found eight." "We might have something here," Pete says, as a white glow appears on the thermal image beneath a tree.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Three months after the fire first ignited, heat is still being detected beneath the ground.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: We make our way towards the coordinates identified by the drone, and at first, there is almost nothing to see.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: A rock Pete picks up from the ground is, too.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Nearby, after scraping away a thin layer of earth, smoke begins to rise.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "It's really now cooking away," Pete says.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "Without the thermal technology we would be totally blind to this." The wildfire began in the middle of July and burned across about 3,300 hectares – 33 sq km – of land, according to the Cairngorms National Park Authority.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: At the height of the emergency, five experienced drone pilots were brought together to provide aerial information to the agencies fighting the fire.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Pete describes it as one of the most challenging environments he has ever flown in, with "multiple walls of flame", personnel and vehicles moving around the site and helicopters operating overhead.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Now the challenge is different.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: The dramatic flames have disappeared, but hot spots can continue to burn beneath the earth.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: This video can not be played On the scene at the Cairngorms wildfire Each one found by the drones is reported to the land manager.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: They send teams who can dig into the ground and douse it with water.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: For Ben Jones, senior site manager for the RSPB at Abernethy, knowing exactly where to send those teams has been crucial.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "We've been fighting this fire for over two months now and obviously we've got limited resources in terms of the number of people we have and we can't send everybody out everywhere all the time," he says.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "So we really need to know where these specific hot spots are - where we should be sending people - so that they can be as efficient as possible." And despite the arrival of colder, wetter weather, the remaining fires cannot simply be ignored.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "Each of these hot spots has got the potential to reignite a larger fire," Ben says.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Walking through the forest, the scale of what happened is almost haunting.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Tree trunks are blackened and charred.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: The acrid smell of fire still hangs around.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Large areas of the forest floor have been scorched.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: But look closely and there are splashes of colour.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Green shoots are emerging.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: I even spot a small yellow flower shooting up from the blackened ground.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Dr Sarah Henshall, head of conservation at the Cairngorms National Park Authority, says it is too early to know the full ecological impact of the fire.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Dr Sarah Henshall says drone information will show how the park is recovering "Some of that will be incredibly quick, some of it will take years, decades, or even beyond our lifetime," she says.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "It will recover, but we just don't know what that's going to look like yet." And the drones that helped during the fire - and are still searching for what remains of it - are being given another job.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Pete is programming them to repeatedly fly exactly the same routes over the damaged landscape.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Using predetermined waypoints, photographs and video can be taken from the same positions month after month and year after year, allowing conservationists to build up a picture of how the landscape changes.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "This standard drone route will have exactly the same route flown month by month, year by year and visually it's going to give us some amazing information about how it's recovering," Sarah says.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: There could be another role for the tech too - spotting future fires before they have a chance to spread.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Pete believes getting a view above the tree canopy quickly could prove critical.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: "It's those moments before a wildfire gets out of control that could be critical to stopping it before it gets out of hand," he says.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Back on the ground, our patrol has found another hot spot.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Again, there is almost nothing visible from a distance.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: But guided by the drone, we find the precise spot.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Beneath a thin layer of earth, it is hot and the smoke becomes obvious after we stoke the soil.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Another location to report.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Another fire for the ground teams to extinguish.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: Above us, the forest is already showing its first signs of life but below our feet, the last of the fire is still burning.
sentences.article_title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms

sentences.text: The channel went live on YouTube on Thursday (BBC News presenter Maryam Moshiri pictured) The BBC News channel has been made available to stream live on YouTube for viewers in the UK and USA.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: The trial, which began on Thursday , external , has been described by BBC bosses as "a significant step" in expanding access to "trusted, impartial journalism in more places people use every day".
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: The move is an expansion of what the BBC has already done in other countries, with the news channel also available to YouTube viewers in Australia, Kenya, Nigeria, and Poland.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: Broadening access to the service forms part of the BBC's wider strategy to reach digitally-native new and younger audiences.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: The channel offers rolling coverage of international and domestic news, as well as breaking news and the latest developments in the worlds of politics, business, technology, culture and sport.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: The BBC's YouTube strategy is widely seen a response to the increasing fragmentation of audiences.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: The guarantees that viewers sit down and turn on their favourite channel - whatever is on it - are long gone.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: Now, their TV sets take them into a world of infinite choice and the BBC (along with the UK's other public service broadcasters) knows it needs to go to where audiences are - as well as trying to entice them to its own platforms.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: Streaming giant YouTube is owned by Google Thursday's development is part of the specific drive by the BBC to take its trusted news to audiences who aren't tuning in to the news channel directly or via the iPlayer.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: BBC News's director of AI, innovation and growth, Anjali Kapoor, said in a statement that audiences "increasingly expect news to be available wherever they are, on the platforms they use throughout their day.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: But it also won't hurt in the continuing negotiations over the BBC's charter and its future funding after 2027.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: This is another signal to the government that the BBC takes its mission seriously; that it is the place for trusted, impartial news and that it understands it must make that news available as widely as possible.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: However, viewers in the UK, watching the channel live on YouTube, may not realise they still need a TV licence to do that.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: But with no guardrails around who's watching, no ability - for now anyway - for the BBC to insist you prove you've paid the fee before you can access its YouTube channels (or its own streaming channels), it's going to be hard to enforce.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: In 2023, it merged with BBC World News into one channel called BBC News, which is also available via the broadcaster's iPlayer, website and app.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: Last year, broadcast regulator Ofcom revealed in its annual report that YouTube had become the UK's second most-watched media service, behind only the BBC.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: One in five young viewers were going to the video sharing platform first when they turn on their smart TVs, the country's media watchdog found, while older people were also watching more of its content.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: Earlier this year, the BBC announced a landmark deal with YouTube, which will see the corporation make content that is tailor-made for the video streaming service.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: The new programmes will feature adverts when viewed from outside the UK, generating extra funds for the corporation at a time when its future funding model is being debated.
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: BBC director general Matt Brittin joined the BBC this year after nearly two decades working for leading tech company Google In July, the corporation's new director general described the traditional TV licence model as "a busted flush" and "no longer fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: Former Google executive Matt Brittin told MPs that the licence fee is "yesterday's model".
sentences.article_title: BBC News channel launches on YouTube for viewers in UK and US

sentences.text: He did not specify what he wants to replace it, but he and BBC chair Samir Shah suggested the government should reconsider a compulsory household levy, which it previously ruled out.

sentences.text: The BBC receives most of its funding from the £180-a-year TV licence, but the number of households paying has declined in recent years, and the broadcaster is discussing reform of the system with the government.

sentences.text: Sally Rooney has sold more than six million copies of her novels globally Normal People author Sally Rooney has said her novels will no longer be supplied to booksellers in the UK as a result of her support for Palestine Action.

sentences.text: The Irish novelist said last year she intended to carry on using her royalties to support the group, which is a proscribed terrorist organisation in the UK.

sentences.text: In a statement to BBC News, Rooney said further publication of her work could constitute a "serious criminal offence", so she had agreed with her publisher Faber not to continue supplying her books to UK retailers.
sentences.article_title: Sally Rooney books withdrawn in UK over Palestine Action support

sentences.text: "I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions, and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences," she said.
sentences.article_title: Sally Rooney books withdrawn in UK over Palestine Action support

sentences.text: Ebook editions have already been removed from sale in the UK, although many book shops still have existing stock of physical copies.
sentences.article_title: Sally Rooney books withdrawn in UK over Palestine Action support

sentences.text: TV presenter Davina McCall has said she experienced symptoms similar to "advanced Alzheimer's" following brain surgery.
sentences.article_title: Davina McCall says memory loss after brain surgery was like 'advanced Alzheimer's'

sentences.text: Speaking on Paloma Faith's podcast Mad, Sad and Bad, the 58-year-old described suffering from memory loss while recovering from an operation to remove a benign brain tumour in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Davina McCall says memory loss after brain surgery was like 'advanced Alzheimer's'

sentences.text: "After I'd had my brain tumour taken out, I had advanced Alzheimer's, so I couldn't remember anything," the former Big Brother host told singer and Celebrity Traitors star Faith.
sentences.article_title: Davina McCall says memory loss after brain surgery was like 'advanced Alzheimer's'

sentences.text: "When I came out of the operation, I didn't know I'd had an operation," she recalled.
sentences.article_title: Davina McCall says memory loss after brain surgery was like 'advanced Alzheimer's'

sentences.text: One regular member of staff would ask McCall every day if she could remember their name.
sentences.article_title: Davina McCall says memory loss after brain surgery was like 'advanced Alzheimer's'

sentences.text: "And I'd go, 'I don't know'." The Masked Singer judge had surgery in November 2024 after doctors had found a rare benign tumour, called a colloid cyst, in a health check-up as part of her menopause advocacy work.
sentences.article_title: Davina McCall says memory loss after brain surgery was like 'advanced Alzheimer's'

sentences.text: In November last year she revealed she had also undergone surgery for breast cancer.
sentences.article_title: Davina McCall says memory loss after brain surgery was like 'advanced Alzheimer's'

sentences.text: She called 2025 the "hardest year" for both her and her partner.
sentences.article_title: Davina McCall says memory loss after brain surgery was like 'advanced Alzheimer's'

sentences.text: Speaking about the recovery from her brain surgery, she said: "Michael would come and visit [the hospital] for two hours, and he'd go to the loo and come back, and I'd go, 'Oh my God, you're here', and I didn't know he'd been there.
sentences.article_title: Davina McCall says memory loss after brain surgery was like 'advanced Alzheimer's'

sentences.text: "I couldn't watch a movie for six months because I couldn't remember what had happened in the movie 15 minutes before. [When reading] a book I couldn't remember the page before." A year ago, for the first time since the brain surgery, she noted, she woke up and could remember what she had done the previous day.

sentences.text: Kgomotso Mathekga says a lack of male role models is fuelling violence against women in his neighbourhood "I witness men hitting women all the time," says Kgomotso Mathekga, 30.

sentences.text: "Especially when they are both drunk." "I once had an argument with my girlfriend," he admits, "and I grabbed and slapped her." Mathekga is speaking frankly during a gathering of men aimed at helping reduce the high levels of violence against women in South Africa.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The meeting is held in a narrow street in a Johannesburg informal settlement known as Organic Market.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: It is a maze of corrugated metal shacks and unpaved roads, close to Alexandra township.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Now I feel pain," Mathekga continues.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We broke up and I no longer see my child.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: I feel like I've contributed to the problems in South Africa, instead of being the gentleman that I know I am." At a nearby tavern, a group of men have pulled their chairs into a circle in the dust.

sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The discovery of the bodies of 12 women over three months, in the city of Ekurhuleni, near Johannesburg has reignited questions about the scale of what many people see as being a crisis of violence against women.

sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The country has one of the highest murder rates in the world, with 5,427 people murdered between April and June this year alone.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: In that period, according to the South African Human Rights Commission, 569 women were killed, an average of six a day, and 1,052 others survived attempted murder.

sentences.text: For Bra Steve, part of the solution to the crisis is helping men to understand the issue and take responsibility for their actions.

sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Reflecting on recent weeks, he says more should be done.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The latest measures announced by Ramaphosa, including better street lighting and a review of unsolved cases , are too little, he says, and too late.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "When I think about all of these recent murders in Johannesburg, I get angry.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Back at the tavern, the men's meeting is wrapping up.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'
